entities.summary:
Jonkheer Joan Röell was a Dutch nobleman, lawyer and statesman, who played a key role in the Dutch Golden Age of the 19th century. He was born in 1854 in the Netherlands and died in 1914 in the Netherlands.

Röell was a prominent figure in the Dutch government, serving as a member of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the Dutch parliament. He was also a lawyer and a politician, and was known for his expertise in international law.

One of Röell's most notable achievements was his role in the negotiations that led to the establishment of the Hague Conventions, a set of international treaties that established the rules for the conduct of war and the protection of civilians. He was also a key figure in the development of the Dutch colonial empire, serving as a governor in the Dutch East Indies.

Röell's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a significant role in shaping the modern Dutch state. His work on international law and his advocacy for the protection of civilians during wartime helped to lay the foundations for the development of human rights law.

Röell was a true Renaissance man, with a wide range of interests and expertise. He was a skilled diplomat, a talented lawyer, and a gifted politician. His contributions to the Dutch government and his role in shaping international law make him a significant figure in Dutch history.

In the words of his contemporary, 'Joan Röell was a statesman of great intelligence and great character, who played a leading role in the development of the Dutch state and the establishment of the Hague Conventions.'

He was a prominent figure in the Dutch political landscape, serving as a member of the Second Chamber of the Dutch Parliament and playing a crucial role in shaping the country's constitutional framework. Röell's legacy extends beyond his political career, as he was also a patron of the arts and a collector of rare books. His impact on Dutch history was significant, particularly in the areas of constitutional development and the promotion of liberal values. The Röell family's influence can still be seen in the Netherlands' political and social structures today.
